name: Spindle-Gyre
description: Spindle-Gyre rotates at a rate that should be impossible for its mass, completing a full revolution in just under six standard hours. This frantic spin has elongated the planet into a pronounced oblate spheroid, its equator bulging outward while the poles are visibly flattened. The atmosphere is a toxic maelstrom of ammonia and methane, its cloud bands wound so tightly they resemble thread on a spindle, spiraling from pole to equator in hypnotic geometric patterns.

The magnetic field generated by this rapid rotation is extraordinarily powerful, creating radiation belts that extend millions of kilometers into space and render close approach suicidal without military-grade shielding. Perpetual hurricanes scream around the equatorial bulge at speeds exceeding ten thousand kilometers per hour, their lightning discharges visible as continuous flickering even from extreme orbital distance. The planet emits a low-frequency electromagnetic hum that crews have described as deeply unsettling, a droning tone that seems to resonate in the bones.

A navigation beacon was placed in high orbit during the early exploration era, and it remains one of the most critical waypoints in the sector. The beacon's maintenance logs record a steady increase in magnetic anomalies near the poles, where the field lines converge with unusual intensity. Some physicists theorize that the planet's impossible rotation rate is accelerating, and that its eventual disintegration could create a debris field spanning the entire inner system.

Fuel skimming operations at Spindle-Gyre are among the most dangerous in known space, with casualty rates that make insurance companies blanch. Yet the helium-3 concentration in the upper atmosphere is among the highest ever recorded, and desperate times breed desperate pilots. The accelerating rotation has become a matter of sector-wide concern, with evacuation plans being quietly drafted for systems within the projected debris radius.
